skill.name: workhub
skill.description: Workhub organizes project documentation with a docs-first workflow for architecture notes, issues, pull request records, and project guides.
skill.summary: Manage project docs, issues, and PR records as a single source of truth.
skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, TypeScript templates, home-path examples, and multilingual Markdown entropy. I found two real semantic filesystem risks in read and create commands. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Resolve the target path, reject absolute paths and .. segments, and require it to stay under docs/.

remediation.issue: Unbounded issue and PR output paths
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize description and category, reject path separators, and verify writes remain under docs/issues or docs/pr.
Add tests for read, issue creation, and PR creation using traversal and absolute path inputs.

high_findings.title: Path Traversal in Document Read Command
high_findings.description: The read command joins user input with docsRoot and reads the result without a boundary check. A crafted path can expose workspace files.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The target argument reaches readFile through join() and then prints file content. No normalization or docsRoot containment check is present.

high_findings.title: Path Traversal in Issue and PR Creation
high_findings.description: The create commands build paths from description and category without sanitizing separators. Crafted input can write Markdown files outside intended docs folders.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: CLI arguments feed join(), mkdir(), and writeFile() directly. No validation enforces docs/issues or docs/pr containment.

content.value_statement: Project documentation often gets scattered across issues, architecture notes, and change records. Workhub gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured docs workflow.
actual_capabilities: Initializes a docs directory with adr, architecture, issues, and pr folders.
Creates dated issue documents from Markdown templates.
Creates dated PR documents from Markdown templates.
Lists issues and PRs with status information from Markdown content.
Reads selected project documents from the docs folder.
Searches issue and PR Markdown files for matching text.
limitations: It requires Bun or a compatible TypeScript runtime.
It works on local Markdown files and does not sync with GitHub automatically.
It assumes command arguments and project paths are trusted.
It does not enforce schema validation for every document field.

use_cases.title: Plan Implementation Work
use_cases.description: Create a dated issue document with goals, phases, acceptance criteria, and notes before coding starts.

use_cases.title: Maintain Agent Context
use_cases.description: Keep task state in files so Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can reload project context later.

use_cases.title: Record Changes for Review
use_cases.description: Create PR records that link back to issues and capture tests, risks, and rollback plans.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Docs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize the Workhub documentation structure for this repository. Then show me the folders that were created.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Workhub issue for adding dark mode in the frontend category. Include clear phases and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Task State
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the docs structure, list open issues, and summarize which task should be read before the next coding step.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Workhub to read the active issue, update completed phases, create a linked PR record, and summarize remaining risks.

output_examples.input: Create an issue for improving login error handling in the backend category.
output_examples.output: A dated issue document is created under the backend issue folder with goals, phases, acceptance criteria, and notes sections.

output_examples.input: Search project issues and PRs for dark mode.
output_examples.output: A short list of matching issue and PR documents is shown with line references and matching text snippets.

output_examples.input: Create a PR record for the completed frontend build fix.
output_examples.output: A dated PR document is created with sections for background, changes, tests, risks, rollback, and linked issue.

best_practices: Read the active issue before making implementation decisions.
Update issue checklists immediately after completing each phase.
Link every PR record to the issue that explains the task context.
anti_patterns: Do not keep important task state only in chat history.
Do not create duplicate documents for the same decision or task.
Do not use untrusted path input when reading or creating documents.

faq.question: What does Workhub manage?
faq.answer: It manages local Markdown documentation for architecture notes, issues, PR records, and project guides.

faq.question: Does Workhub connect to GitHub?
faq.answer: No. It follows GitHub-style workflows but stores records as local Markdown files.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create new task files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create dated issue and PR documents from the included templates.

faq.question: Can it search documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It searches Markdown files in the issues and PR folders.

faq.question: What should users review before installing?
faq.answer: Users should review the path handling risks in the read and create commands.
